name: Synveil
description: A proprietary neuroactive compound that temporarily synchronizes the BCI and augment sensory outputs of two or more individuals within close proximity, creating a shared sensory loop where tactile, proprioceptive, and augment-mediated inputs are experienced by all linked parties simultaneously. Helix markets a restricted clinical version for physical rehabilitation and couples therapy; the street version is unregulated and lacks the clinical version's safety limiters. At full synchronization, users don't just feel what the other person feels — they feel it through their augments, which amplifies and distorts the input in unpredictable ways.
effects: Full sensory synchronization between linked individuals
Shared proprioceptive awareness — you feel your partner's body position as your own
Augment outputs (strength, sensory data, haptic feedback) shared across the link
Emotional bleed — strong emotions in one user register physically in the other
Tactical coordination benefit: linked combatants react as a single organism
side_effects: Identity dissolution at high doses or long durations
Sensory overload if one linked party is injured
Difficulty distinguishing self from partner post-use (hours to days)
Rare cases of permanent partial sync — ongoing intrusive sensory bleed
Augment incompatibility can cause feedback loops and localized electrical burns
cultural_context: The clinical version, sold under the Helix brand with a prescription, is used in rehabilitation clinics to help amputees bond with new chrome and in couples therapy as an intimacy tool. The street version, called 'Twinning,' is the drug of choice for a particular subculture that considers the dissolution of individual identity to be a spiritual experience. Tactically, small combat units have begun using it for coordination that no comm system can match — the risk is that if one member takes a critical hit, the shared pain can incapacitate the whole group.
story_hooks: Two street soldiers used Twinning so frequently over six months that they are now experiencing permanent partial sync — they feel each other's pain, hunger, and arousal at all times and are slowly going mad, seeking anyone who can reverse it.

A Helix executive is secretly funding a Synveil research program that goes far beyond the clinical application — attempting to create a permanent multi-person sync network of loyal operatives who share a hive-like tactical consciousness.

A black-market Synveil session goes wrong when one of the linked users is remotely assassinated mid-sync, and the other three participants experience the death — and may have absorbed a fragment of the dead person's BCI data, including information someone very powerful wants erased.
